tasks.task: Look up the most recent papers related to 'cs.CL', select one and show its abstract.
tasks.answer: Navigated to the most recent cs.CL papers listing at https://arxiv.org/list/cs.CL/recent (50 recent entries displayed), selected the first/most recent paper 'Elucidating the Design Space of LM Data Attribution' (https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.40655) by clicking its Abstract link, and displayed its abstract. Abstract: Data attribution methods for Language Models (LMs) are typically evaluated using downstream tasks like fact retrieval. However, existing evaluations vary multiple dataset properties simultaneously, making it impossible to isolate exactly why an attribution algorithm fails. To diagnose these failures, we explore the design space of LLM data attribution, with a primary focus on evaluation. We introduce the Controlled Attribution Benchmark (CATT) for fact tracing, in which we fine-tune LLMs on entirely fictitious knowledge, providing unambiguous ground truth for attribution. This synthetic setup allows us to systematically alter one dataset configuration at a time, such as document redundancy and lexical distractors. With this configurable evaluation, we demonstrate that redundancy and distractors consistently degrade attribution performance. Rather than proposing a new estimator, we examine two design choices that are underexplored: the loss used to compute gradients and how per-token attribution scores are aggregated into a document score. We find that the true causal evidence within a training document is highly localized, but standard methods dilute this evidence into noise by averaging attribution scores across the entire document. We find that replacing standard cross-entropy loss gradients with the negative log-odds gradients surfaces the critical tokens from other uninformative ones. We can then aggregate only the top token scores to improve ground truth recall by 35 to 72 percentage points across multiple baselines on our diagnostic benchmark. The negative log-odds correction also generalizes to FTRACE-TREX, improving counterfactual retraining performance for every method we test, by up to 4.9x.

tasks.task: Locate the most recent research paper about 'Algebraic Topology' under Mathematics published on ArXiv. Provide the title of the paper, the name of the authors, and the abstract.
tasks.answer:
Most recent Algebraic Topology (math.AT) paper on arXiv, first entry in the new listings at https://arxiv.org/list/math.AT/new (arXiv:2610.37885):

Title: Complete RO-Graded Tambara Structure of H\underline{\mathbb Z} for cyclic groups

Authors: Dongming Zhang

Abstract: We compute the RO-graded Tambara functor of H\underline{\mathbb{Z}} for every finite cyclic group. We introduce a valuation language for homotopy groups: for prime-power cyclic group equivariant, classes are represented by compatible vertex arrays or by edge arrays. In these coordinates we compute products, restrictions, transfers, Weyl actions, and norms. Then we assemble the results into arbitrary finite cyclic group equivariant case. Besides the computation, we also develop the Tate compression theory, which is used in the computation. The Tate compression diagram cut an equivariant spectra into several layer, which the homotopy group can be describe directly by each layers. From it we also give a filtration for \pi_\star(H\underline{\mathbb{Z}}), compatible with products, restrictions, transfers, Weyl actions, and norms.

Locate the latest research about gravitational waves that were uploaded to ArXiv this week and provide a brief summary of one article's main findings.
tasks.answer: Final Response: Latest gravitational-wave research uploaded to arXiv this week (2026-10-25 to 2026-10-31), located via arXiv advanced search for 'gravitational waves' with the submission-date range restricted to this week and sorted by announcement date newest first (105 results). Selected article: 'Gravitational-Wave Echoes and Greybody Cutoff from Logarithmic Throats at a Marginal-Trapping Threshold' (arXiv:2610.40631, submitted 29 Oct 2026). Main findings: When a static, spherically symmetric configuration is brought close to a marginal-trapping threshold, it develops a long throat. As the nondegenerate minimum of F=1-2m/r approaches zero, F ≃ Δ + β(r−R_M)^2, the proper length across the throat grows as −ln Δ/√β even though local curvature stays finite. The authors study how axial gravitational waves propagate in an effective model of this throat, where the lapse is parametrized as N ∝ F^{s/2}, analyzing the resulting gravitational-wave echo signatures and the greybody cutoff associated with the logarithmic throat geometry.

tasks.task: Find the latest paper on 'machine learning in the Statistics section of ArXiv and provide its abstract.
tasks.answer: Latest paper on 'machine learning' in the Statistics section of ArXiv (sorted by Announcement date newest first): 'An ODE-based Sampler for Discrete Diffusion Models' (arXiv:2610.40618). Abstract: Discrete diffusion models have emerged as a powerful framework for generative modeling of sequential data, offering strong theoretical guarantees and competitive empirical performance. Despite their success, sampling remains computationally expensive due to the need for many iterative denoising steps. In this work, we propose an ODE-based sampler for discrete diffusion models that enables faster generation by solving a continuous-time ordinary differential equation derived from the probability flow of the discrete diffusion process. Our approach draws an analogy between continuous and discrete diffusion, adapting the probability flow ODE framework to the discrete setting. We provide theoretical justification showing that our sampler approximates the true data distribution under mild regularity conditions. Experiments on text and image generation benchmarks demonstrate that our method achieves sample quality comparable to standard ancestral samplers while requiring significantly fewer function evaluations, yielding substantial speedups. Our results open the door to more efficient deployment of discrete diffusion models in practical applications.

tasks.task: Locate the latest paper on ArXiv within the 'Nonlinear Sciences - Chaotic Dynamics' category, summarize the abstract and note the submission date.
tasks.answer: Latest paper in arXiv Nonlinear Sciences - Chaotic Dynamics (nlin.CD): 'Three-Wave Forced Hasegawa--Wakatani Model: Reducing Chaos with Zonal Flows' (arXiv:2610.38792) by P. Haerter, R. L. Viana, I. L. Caldas. Submission date: [Submitted on 28 Oct 2026] (v1 submitted Wed, 28 Oct 2026 20:00:44 UTC). Abstract summary: The paper studies resistive drift-wave turbulence using a three-wave truncation of the Hasegawa-Wakatani equations, comparing two triads that differ only by a small tilt of the long-wavelength mode: one zonal (not drivable by the density gradient) and one a weakly driven drift wave. Period maps in the adiabaticity parameter C vs drive show the zonal triad is almost always regular while the non-zonal triad becomes chaotic. Self-consistent gradient feedback (particle source vs turbulent flux erosion) amplifies this contrast, greatly increasing aperiodic states in the non-zonal triad while keeping them negligible in the zonal one. The non-zonal triad reaches chaos via torus breakdown with intermittency, interior crisis and period-doubling, and with a self-consistent gradient via a Neimark-Sacker bifurcation to a phase-locked torus that breaks down abruptly with hysteresis, with chaos persisting up to the largest drive. None of these routes to chaos exist when the long-wavelength mode is zonal, demonstrating that zonal flows reduce/suppress chaos in this system.

tasks.task: Search for the most recent paper related to non-commutative geometry submitted by an author with the first name John. Provide the title and the abstract.
tasks.answer:
Final Response: Title: Finite spectral triples for the fuzzy torus
Authors: John W. Barrett, James Gaunt
Date: v1 submitted 19 August 2019 (most recent version 30 October 2024)
Abstract: Finite real spectral triples are defined to characterise the non-commutative geometry of a fuzzy torus. The geometries are the non-commutative analogues of flat tori with moduli determined by integer parameters. Each of these geometries has four different Dirac operators, corresponding to the four unique spin structures on a torus. The spectrum of the Dirac operator is calculated. It is given by replacing integers with their quantum integer analogues in the spectrum of the corresponding commutative torus.
